REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u0, u2
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, door_open) -> u2
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, door_open) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, !door_open & has_door_key) -> u1
(u2, !door_open & !has_door_key) -> u0
(u2, else) -> u2
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
(u0, door_open, u2) -> 1.0
(u1, door_open, u2) -> 1.0
(u2, !door_open & has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
feedback:
ACCEPT with one non-blocking blemish.

STRUCTURE/FORMAT: All required headers present (REWARD_MACHINE, STATES, INITIAL_STATE, FINAL_STATES, TRANSITION_FUNCTION, REWARD_FUNCTION). FINAL_STATES is nonempty, every listed state is declared, and the accepting set {u0, u2} is correct for the task: u2 = current gift answered (door open), u0 = no pending obligation; u1 (key held, door not yet opened) is correctly non-accepting, so an episode truncated with an unanswered key ends in a rejecting state, matching the success definition.

SEMANTIC FIDELITY: The 3-state cycle u0 (idle) -> u1 (obligation pending) -> u2 (answered, door open) -> u0/u1 matches the environment lifecycle exactly: the key lands only with empty hands and a shut door (u0 -> u1); the toggle that answers consumes the key and opens the door in the same step, so u1 -> u2 fires on door_open alone (has_door_key is already false then; the two propositions never co-occur); the door auto-shuts 10 steps later, and the explicit conjunctions !door_open & has_door_key -> u1 vs !door_open & !has_door_key -> u0 correctly handle the case where a new key lands at the very shutting step (a key may land 'at the shutting step or later'), preserving the new obligation instead of dropping it. Each answered gift earns exactly one 1.0 via (u1, door_open, u2), mirroring the environment's 1-per-gift payout; no other transition pays the main reward.

COVERAGE: Every state's ordered label list is mutually exclusive and exhaustive with a terminating else; irrelevant events (movement, failed toggles, waiting) fall into per-state else self-loops. All three states are reachable and both final states are reachable; 3 states is compact and faithfully tracks the door-open interval.

REWARD SAFETY: Shaping is dense but bounded: 0.1 on obligation onset (u0->u1 and u2->u1) and 1.0 on discharge, so ~1.1 per answered gift, well within the 3-13 gift bound. The 0.1 cannot be farmed - a new onset requires the previous gift to be answered (or the door auto-shut) and a fresh landing - and an idling agent earns at most 0.1 while the answering policy earns ~13x1.1, so the gradient points at the intended behavior. Omitted reward entries (else self-loops, u2->u0) are correctly read as 0.

MINOR BLEMISH (non-blocking): The transition (u0, door_open) -> u2 with reward 1.0 is unreachable. Given the constraint that the door opens only through a toggle with a carried key, and that the key lands while the door is shut (so u0 always routes to u1 at least one step before any opening), door_open can never become true while the machine is in u0. It therefore cannot fire, causes no reward hacking, and does not change behavior - but for exact fidelity to the stated ordering constraint (door_open cannot precede has_door_key) it should ideally be removed or given 0.0. Cleaning that up would make the machine exact; as written it is safe to use for training.

def has_door_key(env): return env.carrying is not None and env.carrying.type == "key"

def door_open(env): return any(cell is not None and cell.type == "door" and cell.is_open for x in range(env.width) for y in range(env.height) for cell in [env.grid.get(x, y)])

Both are persistent condition propositions describing current state, so the absence of any reference to `previous_valuation` is correct. The code is valid executable Python with no imports, no actions, no mutation of the environment or episode memory, and no side effects.
